Let’s break down the SVG path data:

The path consists of four line segments:  
1. (55.64, 52.68) → (35.52, 57.76)  
2. (35.52, 57.76) → (30.04, 36.05)  
3. (30.04, 36.05) → (50.16, 30.97)  
4. (50.16, 30.97) → (55.64, 52.68)  

This forms a closed quadrilateral (four vertices).  

Now check geometric properties:  
- Opposite sides are not parallel (check slopes).  
- Adjacent sides: lengths differ; no two pairs of adjacent sides equal except possibly two pairs? Let’s check:  
  Segment 1 length: √[(55.64−35.52)² + (52.68−57.76)²] ≈ √[20.12² + (−5.08)²] ≈ √(404.8 + 25.8) ≈ √430.6 ≈ 20.75  
  Segment 2 length: √[(35.52−30.04)² + (57.76−36.05)²] ≈ √[5.48² + 21.71²] ≈ √(30.0 + 471.3) ≈ √501.3 ≈ 22.39  
  Segment 3 length: √[(30.04−50.16)² + (36.05−30.97)²] ≈ √[(−20.12)² + 5.08²] ≈ √(404.8 + 25.8) ≈ √430.6 ≈ 20.75  
  Segment 4 length: √[(50.16−55.64)² + (30.97−52.68)²] ≈ √[(−5.48)² + (−21.71)²] ≈ √(30.0 + 471.3) ≈ √501.3 ≈ 22.39  

So sides: 20.75, 22.39, 20.75, 22.39 — two pairs of equal adjacent sides. That’s the definition of a kite.  

Final answer: (D)
